items.quote: it is requisite that wee treat here a little more largly of the Syderyall or invisible man, to wit, of his Originall and power
items.note: The author announces a fuller treatment of one subject: the Syderyall or invisible man, his origin and power.

items.quote: If Aristotle had taken notice of this Olympick Spirit, and Galen made more account of it, there had not such errors crept into Philosophy and Physick
items.note: The author holds that neglect of the Olympick Spirit by Aristotle and Galen let errors into philosophy and physick.

items.quote: springing from the heathenish masters of errors to say nothing of Divinity at present
items.note: He calls these sources heathenish masters of errors and sets aside, for now, what they did to divinity.

items.quote: The invisible man or Olimpick Spirit is borne in us after this manner.
items.note: The invisible man and the Olimpick Spirit are given as two names of one thing, and its birth in us is announced.

items.quote: were taken (as hath been sayd) ex LIMO TERRAE
items.note: Points back to an earlier place where Adam and Eve's being taken from the earth was said.

items.quote: ex LIMO TERRAE, out of the dust of the ground or great world
items.note: The Latin phrase is glossed in English as dust of the ground, and the ground is equated with the great world.

items.quote: For the whole frame of the world is collected and reduced into the Microcosm, so that there is nothing to be found in all the world but the same also is in one man.
items.note: Everything in the world is held to be present also in one man, the Microcosm.

items.quote: the Invisible, Insensible, Sydereall body (which is the house or cottage of the Spirits life) is from the Astra's of the Firmament
items.note: The Sydereall body is defined as the house of the spirit's life and is said to come from the Astra's of the Firmament, as the visible body comes from the earth.

items.quote: Thus Adam had two bodies, that is, a visible Elementall, and an invisible Sydereall body.
items.what: two bodies, that is, a visible Elementall, and an invisible Sydereall body
items.note: Man's makeup is set out as a pair of named bodies.

items.quote: an incorporeall Astralick man which moveth, guideth, and performeth all skilfull matters
items.note: Of the two men born in every generation, the invisible Astralick man moves and guides; the visible man is called its organ and instrument.

items.quote: the invisible Sydereall body that is capable of attaining Phylosophy is from the Astra's of the Firmament
items.note: Only the Sydereall body, not the elementary one, is said to be capable of attaining philosophy.

items.quote: so man the little world is distinguished by his skin or out-side from the great world
items.note: Man is one with his parent the great world, set apart from it by his skin as the great world is set apart from the Angelicall world by its shell.

items.quote: That which is sensible and that which is insensible hath a sydereall spirit or a sydereall body in it.
items.note: The margin extends the sydereall spirit or body to all things, sensible and insensible.

items.quote: Eve is Adam transplanted. The first men were created, the rest proceed from the Being of the seed or Esence.
items.note: The margin separates the created first pair from later men who come from seed; seed is equated with Esence.

items.quote: The Spirit of life is the Spiracle or breathing hole.
items.note: The margin defines the Spirit of life as the Spiracle, glossed as breathing hole.

items.quote: The body of the Limbus & spiracle ought to make one Marriage
items.note: Marriage and adultery are used of the joining of the Limbus body and the spiracle, a figurative use of the words.

items.quote: For as in all thing the marriage or joynting together of two is the perfection
items.note: The joining of two is stated as perfection in all things.

items.quote: it is a body because bodies are the fruits thereof and without a body such fruit cannot grow
items.name: Paracelsus
items.note: The margin reports what Paracelsus says (the name is partly illegible here) about the element of fire being a body; a writing of his is pointed to with vide.

items.quote: Not onely visible things are bodies, for God created as well visible as invisible bodies of the same power.
items.note: Invisible bodies are held to be as real and powerful as visible ones; the wind is the example.

items.quote: The inner Man ascendeth the inward Heaven.
items.note: An inner man and an inward heaven are paired.

items.quote: This Spirit is tha Doctor of true Astronomy.
items.note: The spirit discussed is named the teacher of true astronomy.

items.quote: the Sydereall, Internall, Olimpick. Incorporeall, or (Gabalis Homo) coagulated or curdled Man is the same with the Firmament of the Astra's
items.note: A string of names for one man, including Gabalis Homo glossed as coagulated or curdled man, all said to be the same with the Firmament.

items.quote: as hath been often said
items.note: Points back to earlier places saying this inner man is the same with the Firmament.

items.quote: like rednesse with wine, whitenesse with snow, or the lustre of the Sun with the Aire
items.note: Three likenesses show how the inner man is one with the Firmament: as a quality is one with its thing.

items.quote: this sydereall body is called the Genius of man, because it proceedeth from the Firmament
items.note: Genius is given as a name of the sydereall body, with the reason for the name.

items.quote: it is called Penates, because it is in our power and born with us
items.note: Penates is another name, with its reason.

items.quote: Lar domesticus the good or bad houshould or private Angell
items.note: Lar domesticus is glossed as a good or bad household or private angel.

items.quote: the familiar Homuncle (or little Man) of the Sophies (or wise men,)
items.note: Homuncle is glossed as little man and Sophies as wise men; this is the name the wise men use.

items.quote: Paracelsus his internall Adech (i. e. that which first inwardly formeth in our mind what we afterward outwardly fashion with our hands)
items.name: Paracelsus
items.note: Adech is given as Paracelsus' name for the same thing, with a gloss: what forms inwardly in the mind before the hands make it.

items.quote: the presaging or Propheticall Euestrum that foretelleth any thing by signes
items.note: Euestrum is defined as the prophetic power that foretells by signs.

items.quote: It is also called ahe imagination, which incloseth all the Astra's, and is indeed all the Astra's or Starrs
items.note: Imagination is named as one more name of the sydereall body, and said to be all the Astra's.

items.quote: by which I do not meane the seaven visible coales of Heaven which are but the bodyes of the Astra's but I meane the invisible and insensible body of all things or Astrall Spirit
items.note: The author says his word Astra's is not meant plainly as the visible stars, which are only their bodies, but as the invisible body of all things.

items.quote: they are nothing else but the verue or powers of the Angells
items.note: The Astra's are further defined as the powers of the angels.

items.quote: The Angells which live only upon the vision of God, are the created wisdome of God
items.note: Angels are called the created wisdom of God.

items.quote: he that knowes God, he knows the Astra's also: He that knowes the Astra's cannot but knowe the world, and consequently man the off-spring of the world
items.note: A chain of knowledge: God, then the Astra's, then the world, then man.

items.quote: The Astra's form & bring forth all bodily things out of themselves, and multiply themselves together with those bodily things that are brought forth
items.note: The Astra's are held to produce all bodily things and to multiply with them.

items.quote: the seeds of any graine or Wheat is the Astrum, viz. the invisible body, which being cast into the Earth it produceth a visible body
items.note: The seed is named the Astrum, the invisible body that yields a visible body when sown.

items.quote: the Astrum is nothing else but the insensible, invisible body, or living Spirit, yet without Reason in things that grow; but with reason in living things, as in man
items.note: Astrum is defined as the invisible body or living spirit, without reason in plants, with reason in man.

items.quote: Bodyes are nothing else but the Excrement of the Astra's
items.note: Bodies are called the excrement of the Astra's, brought forth by their operation.

items.quote: This every Astrum can doe of it selfe, as by imagination to bring forth of it selfe another Astrum in a body
items.note: Each Astrum is said to beget another in a body by imagination.

items.quote: There is no body without an Astrum
items.note: Every body has an Astrum; the sentence goes on that no Astrum is without a visible body.

items.quote: The eating of the apple produceth this body the sydereall seed into force & vigour.
items.note: The margin ties the eating of the apple to the sydereall seed coming into force.

items.quote: Astrum, Vulcanus and Archaeus are the same thing, & but one Spirit yet without Reason
items.note: Three names are made one: Astrum, Vulcanus and Archaeus.

items.quote: but one Spirit yet without Reason
items.note: The margin calls the Astrum a spirit without reason; MICRO.32 says the Astrum is without reason in growing things but with reason in living things, as in man.

items.quote: The inner Man is Heaven it selfe or all the Astras.
items.note: The inner man is equated with heaven and all the Astra's.

items.quote: Read in Picus how Trimethius put upon himselfe the various Evestra's of the three-fold world one after another, & transformed himselfe into several shapes
items.name: Trimethius
items.note: The margin points to a writing of Picus telling how Trimethius took on Evestra's and changed shape.

items.quote: by reall Magick he shewed to that great Picus the hidden virtue or power of Man
items.note: Man's power is called hidden, shown to Picus by real magick.

items.quote: We are transformed into that which we most intently gaze and meditate upon.
items.note: What one fixes the mind on, one becomes.

items.quote: The Astra's send the plague into us through our skin as the Sun doth his beams thhrough the glasse.
items.note: Plague is said to come from the Astra's through the skin.

items.quote: whereas the imagination of Man is not one, but all the Astra's, it is as true that it produceth not onely one, but many operations
items.note: Because imagination is all the Astra's, it is said to produce many operations.

items.quote: the Gate of Wonders, the spring and originall of all Magicall operations
items.note: Heightened imagination is named the Gate of Wonders and the source of all magical operations; the sentence before it reads as garbled in the text given.

items.quote: hath power to beget and bring forth visible bodies without detriment or diminution of the Astrall and sydereall Spirit
items.note: Imagination is held to make visible bodies without loss to the spirit, present or absent.

items.quote: The Light of Nature makes bodily things visible, but Eternall things are to be seen onely by Faith
items.note: Two ways of seeing: Light of Nature for bodily things, faith for eternal things.

items.quote: The child in the mothers womb is strangely marked by the impression of the imagination without any bodily touch
items.note: The marking of an unborn child is given as evidence of imagination acting without touch.

items.quote: Thus the Imagination breedeth the Plague and such like Firmamentall diseases; it brings sicknesse and health.
items.note: Imagination is named a cause of plague and of both sickness and health.

items.quote: the Sydereall and Animall Spirit (which is the mechanick Astrall Spirit)
items.note: The Sydereall and Animall Spirit is glossed as the mechanick Astrall Spirit.

items.quote: The Pestilence which comes by fear, trouble and terrour, riseth by the imagination of the Spirit of the lesser world
items.note: Pestilence from fear is traced to the imagination of the sydereall spirit.

items.quote: This sydereall Spirit which is born of the Astra's together with Man (and therefore remains united to the Astra's) is the Load stone and hath a magnetick nature in man.
items.note: The sydereall spirit is called the Load stone of man, with a magnetic nature.

items.quote: The sydereall body and spirit attract unto them the force of the Astra's, as we see in those that are Lunatick
items.note: Lunatics are given as evidence that the sydereall body draws the force of the Astra's.

items.quote: This fourth kind of Naturall Magick called Gamahaea doth all things invisibly and spiritually, by the help of Art
items.what: fourth kind of Naturall Magick called Gamahaea
items.note: A named, numbered kind of natural magick; it does by art invisibly what nature does visibly.

items.quote: This fourth kind of Naturall Magick
items.note: Calling this the fourth kind points to other kinds named elsewhere in the writing; the lines given do not show them.

items.quote: The House is as it were dead, but the Inhabitant to wit, the Spirit of perpetuall motion of invisible Nature or the magnetick spark of the Soule of the world liveth and worketh effectually
items.note: House and inhabitant stand for body and indwelling spirit, flagged with as it were and to wit.

items.quote: workmanship, Arts, Sciences, and the knowledge of all things lie hid in the Astra's of the Firmament
items.note: All wisdom, arts and knowledge are said to lie hidden in the Astra's.

items.quote: There is nothing so hidden in the world which is not praefigured in the Astra's
items.note: Whatever is hidden in the world is prefigured in the Astra's.

items.quote: all the Astra's of the Firmament, which are the Tincture of the speculation of our mind
items.note: The Astra's are called the Tincture of the mind's speculation.

items.quote: can of their own in-bred or naturall force by imagining produce bodily and visible things out of that which doth not appear
items.note: The Astra's make visible things from the invisible by imagining; a sudden cloud yielding rain and hail is the example.

items.quote: all things in the first Creation were produced out of the DIVINE NOTHING, or invisible Cabalisticall Poynt, into something
items.note: The DIVINE NOTHING is equated with the invisible Cabalisticall Poynt from which creation came.

items.quote: All things proceeded out of the invisible Darknesse, and were called out to the visible Light by the WORD speaking, and the Spirit cherishing.
items.note: Creation runs from invisible darkness to visible light through the Word and the Spirit.

items.quote: it must needs be that the Firmament also hath an Imagination but without Reason, as Man the off-spring of the world hath with Reason
items.note: The Firmament is held to have imagination without reason; man has it with reason. Nettle and fire are the example.

items.quote: the Astra's do those things which Humane wisdom desireth
items.note: The Astra's carry out what human wisdom desires; the margin links wisdom with enchantment.

items.quote: Heaven knoweth all things most certainly, all actions and events of Men are pictured in the Astra's
items.note: All human actions and events are said to be pictured beforehand in the Astra's.

items.quote: is a three fold NIHIL or Nothing, a Divine, Privative and Negative NOTHING
items.note: A threefold Nothing is distinguished: divine, privative and negative; the subject word is illegible.

items.quote: The whole Heaven is nothing else but the Imagination
items.note: Heaven is equated with the Imagination.

items.quote: whereas Man is the Quintessence of the greater world, it follows that Man may not onely imitate Heaven, but rule it also at his beck
items.note: Because man is the Quintessence of the world, he can imitate and rule heaven.

items.quote: All things naturally obey the Soule, and must of necessity move and work toward that which the soule earnestly desireth
items.note: Natural things obey the soul when it desires vehemently.

items.quote: when by holinesse we draw vertue from him who is the true Archetype, and when we ascend to him, then every Creature must and will obey us
items.note: The power over creatures is conditioned on holiness and ascent to God, the true Archetype.

items.quote: By the help of Imagination all Magicall operations and all wonderfull things are done through the Naturall inborn Faith
items.note: Magical operations are done by imagination through natural inborn faith.

items.quote: The Imagination worketh in Man like the Sun
items.note: Imagination is compared to the sun working without an instrument.

items.quote: The Imagination of Man is the Loadstone that attracteth above a 1000 miles off
items.note: Imagination is called a loadstone drawing from great distance and, exalted, drawing what it will from the elements.

items.quote: unles first it attract the thing conceived by the attractive force of the imagination, that it may beget the Architect of the Imagination as a native spirit out of it selfe
items.note: First step of how imagination works: it attracts the thing conceived and begets from itself the Architect of the Imagination.

items.quote: afterward the Imagination being as it were with child maketh impression, which though it be not tangible, yet it is corporeall like the wind
items.note: Second step: the imagination, as if pregnant, makes an impression, intangible yet bodily like the wind.

items.quote: By Faith we may do good or evillus God permitteth.
items.note: Faith can work good or evil, as God permits.

items.quote: the true Magician or wise Man can attract the operation of the Astra's, stones, mettalls, &c. into the Imagination
items.note: The wise man draws the operation of the Astra's, stones and metals into the imagination, as a burning glass draws the sun's heat.

items.quote: the true Magician or wise Man
items.note: Magician is equated with wise man.

items.quote: Thus by Imagination and true Gabalia all hearbs, all growing things, all mettalls may be produced.
items.note: Herbs, growing things and metals can be produced by imagination and true Gabalia.

items.quote: This part of Magick is called Gabalisticall, and is supported with three Pillars.
items.what: This part of Magick is called Gabalisticall
items.note: A named part of magick with three pillars, listed in the next paragraphs.

items.quote: Magick or Faith transplanting minds hath power over all Spirits and Ascendants.
items.note: Magick is equated with faith that transplants minds.

items.quote: First, with TRUE PRAYERS made in Spirit and Truth
items.note: First pillar of Gabalisticall magick.

items.quote: when God is prayed unto in the internall Spirit, not with noyse of words, but in a sacred silence, without opening the mouth and groaning
items.note: How the prayer is done: inwardly, silently, without speech.

items.quote: Secondly, by NATURALL FAITH, or in-born Wisdome
items.note: Second pillar, equated with in-born wisdom, given by God equally to all men at the Creation.

items.quote: Thirdly, by a strongly exalted IMAGINATION
items.note: Third pillar.

items.quote: as well in Jacobs Rods mentioned by Moses
items.name: Moses
items.note: Jacob's rods, as Moses tells them, are cited as evidence of imagination's force; the margin gives Gen. 30.37.
The margin names the place in Genesis for Jacob's rods.

items.quote: as in pregnant women who imprint the mark of that which they long for upon the child, as hath been said
items.note: Points back to the marking of the unborn child said earlier (MICRO.33, MICRO.34).

items.quote: The Imagination or Fantasie of Man is like the Load stone in its Nature, attracting the Fantasie of other men, as we see in those that gape and yawn.
items.note: Imagination draws other men's fantasy; yawning is the example.

items.quote: A vehement Imagination doth not onely cause a transmutation of ones own body, but sometimes also of anothers, by way of imitation
items.note: Vehement imagination can transmute one's own body and another's, through likeness.

items.quote: Many by their melancholly Imagination and diffidence have exposed themselves to the temptation of the uncleane Spirit
items.note: A melancholy imagination and distrust lay men open to the unclean spirit.

items.quote: have so prevailed that on a sudden they have become the Temples of the living God
items.note: Intent imagination with firm faith, hope and prayer makes men temples of God; the counterpart of MICRO.42.

items.quote: True Faith is the cure of a false Imagination. Many fall sick and recover againe by the Faith of Imagination.
items.note: Faith cures false imagination; sickness and recovery come by the faith of imagination.

items.quote: The Sum of all is, that we worship God devoutly in honesty and holinesse
items.note: The author gives the sum of the whole matter as devout worship of God.

items.quote: as the more secret Theosophers or wise-hearted to God well know
items.note: The knowledge is ascribed to the more secret Theosophers, glossed as the wise-hearted to God.

items.quote: the Understanding or Mind flaming with a Religious love, is joyned to the separated Intelligences
items.note: Devout prayer joins the mind to the separated Intelligences.

items.quote: uniteth the mind with God, and learneth and knoweth all things of God
items.note: Internal prayer unites the mind with God and gives knowledge of all things.

items.quote: by reason of worldly cares and thoughtfulnesse wherewith they are overwhelmed, they can doe nothing that favoureth of true Wisdome
items.note: Worldly cares keep even those who know this disposition from acting on it.

items.quote: Such like contemplations as these which are of greatest Antiquity will seem harsh and crabbed to the rude and vulgar sort of men; for few read them, and fewer understand them
items.note: These contemplations are said to be for few readers and to seem harsh to the vulgar.

items.quote: they require a larger narration then can be made of them at this time. To returne therefore to our purpose.
items.note: The author breaks off the digression, saying the matter needs fuller treatment than he gives now, and returns to his purpose.

items.quote: The purified Mind, like a river, entereth into the very inmost secrets of things, beyond all shadowes.
items.note: The purified mind reaches the inmost secrets of things.

items.quote: It is of greatest concernment that all Chymists should bewell acquaintedwith this true Fundamentall of the occult Phylosophycal Physick
items.note: The author tells chymists they must know this foundation, which he calls occult philosophical physick.

items.quote: because of the Harmonicall concord and conspiration between the superiour and inferiour things of the greater and lesser world
items.note: The reason given is the accord between higher and lower things of great and little world.

items.quote: Petrus Severinus the Dane, together with Pratensis that faithfull Achates, deserveth to be numbred among the Ancient wise men
items.note: The author praises Severinus, after Paracelsus, for clearing this foundation in his Idaea of Paracelsean Physick.

items.quote: my honoured friend Joseph Quercetan Councellour and most worthy Physitian to the King of France
items.note: Quercetan, called his friend, is named as having confuted Severinus' adversaries.

items.quote: Th: Bovius an Italian of Verona, and Th: Muffet an Englishman, the best Hermetick Physitians of this age
items.note: Bovius and Muffet are praised as the best Hermetick physicians of the age.
